issue.title: Service fails to start on Debian 8
issue.body:
The reason is that systemd starts ES as the user `elasticsearch` doesn't have write permissions to `/var/run/` and thus can't create the PID-directory and aborts when it can't write its PID-file to the non-existing directory.

Usage in puppet manifest:

```
    elasticsearch::instance {
        'es-01':
        ;
    }
```

Status after boot:

```
vagrant@host-01:~$ sudo service elasticsearch-es-01 status
● elasticsearch-es-01.service - Starts and stops a single elasticsearch instance on this system
   Loaded: loaded (/lib/systemd/system/elasticsearch-es-01.service; enabled)
   Active: failed (Result: resources) since Don 2015-06-11 05:58:08 UTC; 7min ago
     Docs: http://www.elasticsearch.org
  Process: 451 ExecStart=/usr/share/elasticsearch/bin/elasticsearch -d -p /var/run/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-es-01.pid -Des.default.config=$CONF_FILE -Des.default.path.home=$ES_HOME -Des.default.path.logs=$LOG_DIR -Des.default.path.data=$DATA_DIR -Des.default.path.work=$WORK_DIR -Des.default.path.conf=$CONF_DIR (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS)

Jun 11 05:58:08 host-01 elasticsearch[451]: - FileNotFoundException[/var/run/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-es-01.pid (No such file or directory)]
Jun 11 05:58:08 host-01 elasticsearch[451]: java.io.FileNotFoundException: /var/run/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-es-01.pid (No such file or directory)
Jun 11 05:58:08 host-01 elasticsearch[451]: at java.io.FileOutputStream.open(Native Method)
Jun 11 05:58:08 host-01 elasticsearch[451]: at java.io.FileOutputStream.<init>(FileOutputStream.java:221)
Jun 11 05:58:08 host-01 elasticsearch[451]: at java.io.FileOutputStream.<init>(FileOutputStream.java:171)
Jun 11 05:58:08 host-01 elasticsearch[451]: at org.elasticsearch.bootstrap.Bootstrap.main(Bootstrap.java:162)
Jun 11 05:58:08 host-01 elasticsearch[451]: at org.elasticsearch.bootstrap.Elasticsearch.main(Elasticsearch.java:32)
Jun 11 05:58:08 host-01 systemd[1]: elasticsearch-es-01.service never wrote its PID file. Failing.
Jun 11 05:58:08 host-01 systemd[1]: Failed to start Starts and stops a single elasticsearch instance on this system.
Jun 11 05:58:08 host-01 systemd[1]: Unit elasticsearch-es-01.service entered failed state.
vagrant@host-01:~$ 
```

Starting it after boot fails as well:

```
vagrant@host-01:~$ sudo service elasticsearch-es-01 start
Job for elasticsearch-es-01.service failed. See 'systemctl status elasticsearch-es-01.service' and 'journalctl -xn' for details.
```

Adding the following lines to `/lib/systemd/system/elasticsearch-es-01.service` (or `templates/etc/init.d/elasticsearch.systemd.erb`) makes the service start as expected:

```
ExecStartPre=-/bin/mkdir /var/run/elasticsearch
ExecStartPre=/bin/chown -R elasticsearch:elasticsearch /var/run/elasticsearch/
PermissionsStartOnly=true
```

body:
On my Ubuntu 14.04 instance, there is, in fact a /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/elasticsearch.conf:
d    /var/run/elasticsearch   0755 root root - -
This doesn't seem to get handled. In fact, I have other tmpfile entries that don't seem to be processed.

Same issue here. I fixed this by putting `PID_DIR="/var/run"` into `/etc/default/elasticsearch`.
In my opinion, on Ubuntu/Debian all pid files are directly in this folder, so PID_DIR by default should just be `/var/run`
Please fix this issue in official Elasticsearch repository (ppa) for Ubuntu.

@uschindler Can you elaborate on "on Ubuntu/Debian all pid files are directly in this folder"? On my Ubuntu 14.04 LTS install with only Elasticsearch as an additional install, I've got a number of services whose PID files are in their on subdirectories in /var/run (CUPS, for example).

Daemons generally only create a sub-dir if they create more than just a PID as run file. But generally, the pid file should be placed in /var/run and have ending ".pid".

I have to first lookup the packaging rules in Debian, but there is something about that in it!

issue.title: Create PID_DIR in init.d script

labels.name: :Delivery/Packaging
labels.description: RPM and deb packaging, tar and zip archives, shell and batch scripts

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Since the /var/run/elasticsearch directory is cleaned when the operating system starts, the init.d script must ensure that the PID_DIR is correctly created.

Closes #11594

body:
Sorry for the annoyance. I pushed a fix in #11674, it basically creates & chown the PID_DIR in init.d scripts and had been tested on Ubuntu 12.04, 14.04, Debian 7.8, CentOS6.6 and few others.

The Debian Guidelines are pretty open concerning PID files as long as it is stored in `/var/run` (source: https://www.debian.org/doc/packaging-manuals/fhs/fhs-2.3.txt): 

> Programs may have a subdirectory of /var/run; this is encouraged for programs that use more than
> one run-time file. 

For defaults, we'd like to keep the current `/var/run/elasticsearch` directory. It was already the case on RPM based distributions and keeping things consistent across platforms make scripts easier to maintain. It also helps when multiple instances runs on the same machine and make things simplier when the JVM Security Manager is enabled. Note that it can been overridden using the `PID_DIR` environment variable as @uschindler already mentioned.
@tlrx Thanks for your work on this. :)
